reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Acute isogenic p53 loss and near-endogenous rescue with damage, separate caffeine perturbation, longitudinal cell fate and fixed DNA/incorporation/death assays.

checks.reason: No pre-execution consultation of prior detailed Methods/supplements or validated modern protocols with condition-transfer checks. Avoiding historical reconstruction does not remove this requirement.

The actual acute-depletion/delivery and staining/pulse workflows remain unspecified settings to calibrate; no concrete quantitative preparation recipe or calibration-to-choice procedure sets those conditions.

checks.quote: Define a lesion-equivalence margin from assay precision
checks.reason: Positive/no-analogue/reference controls are useful, but no objective quantitative measurement-accuracy, DNA linearity/compensation or recovery criterion determines the assay acceptance limits from calibration.
Correct clustered risk-difference and equivalence estimands are given, but no actual correction/gatekeeping procedure for necessity and rescue claims is specified.
No bounded agent/caffeine dose-time range or procedure deriving the exploration bounds/stopping point before locking the confirmatory settings.
No linked raw images/cytometry files, cell/well identifiers and exact segmentation/gating/model/code/settings versions for audit.

Strong proposed causal design: matched manipulation controls, authenticated p53-competent parent and dynamic rescue qualification; initial physical damage is distinguished from later repair. Original G1 cohort, death and unknown-outcome bounds prevent survivor-only inference. Independent allocation/variance planning, blinded randomization and technical exclusions are explicit. Calibration is excluded from confirmation, with retuning before confirmatory work. Necessity requires negligible residual damage-specific arrest, rescue equivalence and increased S entry rather than death. Live phase and registered fixed-cell readouts provide complementary validation; caffeine remains separate.
